title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'magma' M of 'figures', meaning pieces of a tame or polyhedral space, by order-theoretic primitive relations instead of point sets. After several revisions he settled, on the previous page, on three primitives:
- X ≤ Y: a closure or face-type order. A proper X ≤ Y has interior disjoint from Y (Mag 4').
- X ≪° Y: an 'interior containment' order. It is disjoint from ≤ except at equality: (X ≤ Y ∧ X ≪° Y) ⟺ X = Y.
- X |∘| Y: symmetric and antireflexive, read as 'interiors disjoint'.
He calls this choice 'l'épurement intégral'.

This page does two things.

(1) It notes that the choice of primitives (≤, ≪°, |∘|) dictates the corresponding choice for an auxiliary set F. Of the three relations, only ≤ transfers to F. From F's own point of view it is better to present the structure as (M, F | ◁, ≪°, |∘|). Here ◁ is an incidence relation between M and F, and ≪°, |∘| are relations on M; ≤ on M and on F is then derived through ◁. This is a two-sorted, incidence-geometry style presentation of the same structure.

(2) It specializes to 'strictly divisible' magmas (cf. §7). The margin glosses this, probably, as 'magmas où L est très dense'. Define L = {X ∈ M | X minimal for ≤ and for ≪°}, the atoms or 'points'. Then |∘| becomes redundant: it is determined by a symmetric, antireflexive relation || ('apartness') on L. The structure reduces to (M, ≤, ≪°, ||) with three axioms:
- Mag div 1: ≤ and ≪° are orders on M, and || is symmetric and antireflexive on L.
- Mag div 2: as Mag 2', i.e. the compatibilities between ≤ and ≪°.
- Mag div 3: if X ≤ Y, X ≠ Y, x ≪° X, y ≪° Y, with x, y ∈ L, then x || y.
The margin recovers |∘| from || roughly as X |∘| Y ⟺ (for the atoms x ≪° X, y ≪° Y) x || y. So disjointness of interiors is read off from apartness of the atoms lying in the interiors, which is what 'L dense' should guarantee.

The next page continues the hierarchy:
- 'quasi-ensembliste' magmas: every figure has an interior atom;
- 'ensembliste' magmas: X |∘| Y ⟺ X° ∩ Y° = ∅;
- a summary table of axiom systems (atomic, mixed, divisible, quasi-set, set-theoretic, polyhedral).

Purpose: a point-free, combinatorial foundation for 'tame topology', the program sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5. Here genuine points (L) are recovered from regions only under a density hypothesis.
errors: The marginal formula X |∘| Y ⟺ ... x || y is ambiguous as to quantifiers. With an existential quantifier ('∃ x ≪° X, y ≪° Y with x || y') it would not express interior-disjointness; it should be universal (all interior atoms of X are apart from all interior atoms of Y), plus a density assumption so that every figure has interior atoms. The image seems compatible with a universal reading.

Mag div 3 gives only one direction of the link between |∘| and ||, deduced from Mag 4' (proper ≤ implies |∘|). Showing that |∘| is fully redundant needs the converse and density (the 'strictly divisible' hypothesis of §7, not on this page). This is not checked here.
The role of F and of the incidence ◁ is only sketched. F (possibly closed figures or faces) is not defined on this page, and the derivation of ≤ from ◁ is not written out.

ideas.what: Primitive relations on regions: part-of/face order ≤, interior containment ≪°, and interior-disjointness |∘|, axiomatized without points
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / region-based (point-free) topology; contact algebras; non-tangential proper part (RCC8), 'well inside' relation of proximity spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992); Efremovich proximity (1951); Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the program of tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5; the axiomatics are unpublished

ideas.what: Two-sorted presentation (M, F | ◁, ≪°, |∘|) with an incidence relation between M and F, from which ≤ on both sorts is derived
ideas.modern_name: Incidence structure / two-sorted (Chu-space-like) presentation of a region structure

ideas.what: Points recovered as doubly minimal elements L, with |∘| reduced to an apartness relation || on L when L is 'dense' (strictly divisible magmas)
ideas.modern_name: Atoms / points of an atomic mereotopology; apartness relation; representation theorems for contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Representation theory of contact/proximity algebras (Düntsch–Winter, Dimov–Vakarelov); apartness spaces (Bridges–Vîță)

ideas.what: Hierarchy of axiom systems: general → strictly divisible → quasi-set-theoretic → set-theoretic magmas, plus a polyhedral variant
ideas.modern_name: Classification of region-based structures by atomicity/density
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous hierarchies (atomic vs atomless mereology) in the philosophical-logic literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics use essentially the primitives of mereotopology and contact/proximity algebras. ≪° plays the role of non-tangential inclusion or 'well inside', |∘| that of external contact / interior-disjointness, and L with || that of atoms with apartness. These were developed independently in AI spatial reasoning (RCC, 1992) and in the logic of contact algebras. The two literatures have not been connected.
missed.quote: (M, F | ◁, ≪°, |∘|) ... L = {X ∈ M | X minimal pour ≤ et pour ≪°}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Representation theorems for contact algebras, and the decidability of RCC fragments, could shed light on the point-recovery problem Grothendieck addresses ('strictly divisible' vs 'set-theoretic' magmas), and vice versa for polyhedral/tame models.

missed.claim: The claim that for strictly divisible (L-dense) magmas the interior-disjointness relation is redundant, being determined by an apartness on the atoms, is stated but neither proved nor made precise. The incidence version with F is left as a sketch.
missed.quote: La relation |∘| est ici redondante, sur M, on a la donnée d'une relation || sur L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A precise representation theorem for such 'magmas' would be a point-free foundation for tame or o-minimal-like topology, as envisaged in the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished, carefully revised point-free axiomatization of 'tame' regions by Grothendieck that closely parallels mereotopology/contact algebras, a parallel absent from the literature. The page itself is an intermediate axiom-tuning step with no proved theorem.
transcription_corrections: Left margin gloss is likely '*Magmas où L est très dense' rather than 'Magmas ou liens très denses'.
Line 3 likely reads 'fixe la main, pour ainsi dire, pour le choix correspondant pour F ...' rather than 'fixe les axiomes'. Uncertain.
Marginal formula: the quantifiers appear to be over all x ≪° X, y ≪° Y (i.e. X |∘| Y ⟺ ∀ x ≪° X, ∀ y ≪° Y, x || y) rather than a single '∃'. Uncertain.
The struck text at the end of Mag div 3 is cancelled (illegible) and should not be read as content.
